note: Brythonic Strathclyde absorbed into expanding Scottish realm over eleventh century; dates approximate.

_quarry.structural_significance: The absorption of Strathclyde's Brittonic kingdom into Scotland extinguished the last continuous P-Celtic polity in mainland Britain; the linguistic displacement of Cumbric by Gaelic and later Scots represents the final stage in the replacement of Romano-British political culture by the Gaelic-influenced Scottish kingdom that defined medieval northern Britain.
